name: Iowa

statute.name: Iowa Open Records Law (Chapter 22)
statute.citation: Iowa Code ch. 22 (§ 22.2 right to examine; § 22.3 copies; § 22.8(4)(d) delay)

response.rule_text: A reasonable delay to decide whether a confidential record can be released 'should not exceed twenty calendar days and ordinarily should not exceed ten business days', Iowa Code § 22.8(4)(d); the limit is not absolute (Horsfield Materials).

fees.labor_rule: Custodian may charge a reasonable fee for supervision of records examined, Iowa Code § 22.3.
fees.copy_rule: Copy fee may not exceed actual cost of providing the service and excludes ordinary overhead such as benefits and depreciation, § 22.3(2).
fees.waiver_rule: No provisions for fee waivers when disclosure serves the public interest.

residency.rule_text: 'Every person' has the right to examine and copy public records, Iowa Code § 22.2(1).

appeal.body: Iowa Public Information Board (complaint) or district court
appeal.rule_text: The Iowa Public Information Board (Iowa Code ch. 23) investigates complaints under chapters 21 and 22 and issues advice or declaratory orders; suit in district court is also available. IPIB has no jurisdiction over the governor's office or the legislative branch.

notes: No general response clock is stored: the 10-business/20-calendar-day figures are an outer limit on the delay to decide whether a confidential record may be released, not a deadline for every request; the rule stays in response.rule_text. IPIB complaint deadline not found. Rehearing text in RCFP (17A.16, 20 days) concerns agency final decisions, not IPIB records complaints. Governor: act treats governor as covered but IPIB lacks jurisdiction; executive privilege claimed 2025. Universities (ISU Foundation) held subject in case law; school districts not confirmed.
